pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to St Michael’s Prep School
pageCache.text:
Our ethos The Joy and Wonder of Learning
Explore our School
your child's Nursery journey
the Joy and Wonder of Learning
St Michael's Reception
the adventure starts here Follow our Journey
Nursery and Kindergarten
Life begins at St Michael’s in our Nursery and Kindergarten where a lifelong love of learning is nurtured. New skills are developed and the foundation of your child’s education is set.
The adventure continues into Reception where classroom learning and trips to our Forest School are introduced. It is here our children discover and explore the joy and wonder of our natural world.
In Year 1, Swimming & French lessons are introduced. In Year 2, our children enjoy a vibrant programme of transition events which prepare them for the next stage of their journey into the Prep school.
Our Years 3 and 4 pupils are introduced to specialist teachers and weekly sports fixtures. Our lessons, trips and events inspire the children as they enjoy themed Roman, Rock and Egyptian Days.
We recognise that every child is unique and foster their happiness, self-confidence, resilience and well-being. From Year 5, we work closely with you to find a senior school that will suit your child.
Our Years 7 and 8 pupils enjoy a unique curriculum, scholarships, leadership roles and unforgettable trips. These opportunities prepare our children for senior school and life beyond St Michael's.

pageCache.pageTitle: Inspection Reports - St Michael's Prep School
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
ISI Inspection Report Summary, May 2024
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI)* introduced a new framework for inspections in 2023 as part of which they no longer provide a formal overall classification of e.g. excellent/good/satisfactory etc. for a school as they did in the past. The report now advises on whether the ISI Standards are met with all feedback provided in the detailed comments.
We are delighted that St Michael’s Prep School met all the required standards of the May 2024 ISI inspection with the addition of a ‘significant strength’ awarded for St Michael’s ‘strong culture of collaboration and mentorship’ which equips our pupils for life. One example that the inspection team gave of this strength was the St Michael's Challenge ‘which involves pupils from Years 7 and 8 providing useful and valued guidance and mentorship to younger pupils when they carry out research and deliver presentations.’ A significant strength is highlighted by the Independent Schools Inspectorate in rare instances that they identify a strength of provision in a school which results in a ‘clear, demonstrable and highly beneficial impact for pupils.’
The report described St Michael’s Prep School as ‘a place where the school’s motto perseverantia, sapientia, gratia (perseverance, wisdom and gratitude) is brought to life’ with a community which ‘cherishes individuality and celebrates diversity’.
Early years at St Michael’s was identified as a stage where ‘children thrive in an encouraging and caring environment’, the foundations of ‘positive relationships’ are built and ‘children are encouraged to be kind to each other.’ The role of St Michael’s early years team in modelling how to behave was also commended, which the children respond to ‘by working and playing happily together’.
‘High quality teaching and learning resources’ were demonstrated across St Michael’s led by teachers who ‘plan and structure their lessons well’ and have ‘secure subject knowledge’. ISI noted the impact that this has on St Michael’s pupils who are ‘interested in what they are taught’ and ‘readily ask questions to deepen their understanding by capitalising on their teachers’ expertise.’
St Michael’s Years 7 and 8 provision was likewise praised by the inspectors who described our senior pupils as having ‘enthusiasm, confidence and proficiency in their leadership of others’, understanding ‘that the help they give is a service to their community,’
Growth mindset was recognised as an attribute of pupils across all year groups, empowering them to view mistakes as ‘opportunities to learn’. ISI noted that ‘pupils maintain this positive approach to new challenges’ throughout their St Michael’s journey. They recognised the recent focus on five different learning behaviours: collaboration, independence, resilience, creativity and engagement which were developed with pupil, parent and staff focus groups.
The inspection team also praised the enjoyment that pupils gain from their learning at St Michael’s, noting that they ‘make rapid progress throughout the school’ and are ‘prepared well for the next stages of their education both within the school and when the time comes for them to move on’. St Michael’s ‘considerable success in local and national competitions in a range of subjects’ was similarly praised.
Reflecting on the sense of community at St Michael’s, the inspection team acknowledged the ‘ethos of mutual trust and respect for everyone’ which ‘characterises the whole school community’.
Most pleasingly, St Michael’s pupils were described as knowing ‘that their voices and opinions are heard, valued and acted upon.’
ISI Inspection Report May 2024
Regulatory Compliance Inspection January 2020

Educational Quality Inspection March 2017

Pre-School Sports and Music Showcase
On Wednesday, our Nursery and Kindergarten children took part in a super Sports Day and Summer Concert led by Mr Davies and Mrs Crane. The children were amazing, bringing lots of energy, enthusiasm and smiles. It was lovely to see how their hard work and the support of the team came together so beautifully.
A big thank you to all of the parents, grandparents and carers for coming along to watch and support the children, you helped make the day truly special for your little ones.

Governors
Rashid Chinchanwala
Rashid is an Old Michaelian, attending St Michael’s Prep as a boarder from 1972 to 1977 and holding the position of Deputy Head Boy during his time here. He has been a St Michael’s Governor since November 2007.
A chartered accountant, he has worked in finance within the UK media industry for 27 years and has a good working knowledge of film & TV production, media buying and market research. In 2008, he helped found his current business Media Powerhouse Ltd, an audio visual services company which he is the Finance Director of.
Rashid’s interests include mainstream sports, travel and photography.
Julia Tyson
Julia has over 30 years’ experience as a senior HR professional across a diverse range of sectors, having built her early career in Boots, TDG and Marconi before entering Financial Services with both Barclays and RBS during a period of significant corporate restructuring activity. She has held strategic and transformational roles as Group HR Director at Wates in the construction sector and at LV= where she played a major role in promoting both the Talent, Diversity and CSR agenda, winning several prestigious awards including BITC Company of the Year. She is the MD of Beyond People, a change consultancy, a NED of a housing association and a digital learning trust and is a Henley qualified Executive Coach with a focus on leadership team effectiveness.
Kellie Crozer
Kellie began her career in the education sector after completing a B.Ed Primary (Hons) degree. She has worked in both the state and independent sector for over 25 years in various roles including Class Teacher, Phase Leader and Deputy Head. Currently, she is Head of the Nursery and Pre-Preparatory School at King's School Rochester including Head of Early Years and Whole School Safeguard Lead. Kellie has also worked as an Early Years Advisor for Kent County Council where she played a crucial role in shaping early years education policies and practice. She is passionate that all children receive the highest quality education.
She is married and the proud mother of two children – both now of senior school age. Kellie was born and raised in Kent, although lived in North and West London for a while. She moved back to Kent 16 years ago to raise her family and be nearer to her own family. She enjoys walking, theatre, live music and watching (not playing) sport!
She is very keen to get to know the St Michael’s Team and work closely with them.
Susan Ward
Susan was a parent at St Michael’s Prep for three years. Her daughter joined in Year 6 and left at the end of Year 8 with outstanding memories of St Michael’s. Because of this, Susan was keen to stay involved in the school and participate in its future growth.
Susan has over 25 years’ experience in financial services, having worked for both JPMorgan and UBS. Since leaving UBS, Susan has been building an advisory business in impact investing and pursuing various start-up opportunities.
Susan lives in Sevenoaks with her husband and two daughters. Together they enjoy cycling, walking and other outdoor activities in Kent.
Adam Scarff
Adam is an Old Michaelian who joined St Michael’s Prep in 1988 and has remained a regular visitor since. Adam grew up in Otford and moved to Cambridge where he studied after leaving St Michael’s.
Adam now works in the property and construction industry where he runs a bespoke windows and doors company, Valdi ltd. This career choice follows in the footsteps of his grandfather who worked as a cabinet maker when he came to the UK from Poland during the Second World War.
Adam is a proud father of two girls which helps put him in touch with the current needs of the school. In his spare time he enjoys car building and restoration, rugby, hiking and outdoor activities.
He has always been a staunch advocate for the Old Michaelians Association and is looking to revamp and improve the current alumni.
Adam has been a St Michael’s Governor since 2019.
Nick Skelly
Nick is an ex-parent, his children attended St Michael’s Prep School from Nursery through to Prep. He is a keen golfer and enjoys spending his free time on the course. Nick has worked in the construction industry for 27 years as a chartered quantity surveyor. He is highly skilled in his profession and has a wealth of experience in managing construction projects. Nick is a dedicated professional who takes pride in his work and is committed to delivering high-quality results.
Callum Needham
Callum is an Old Michaelian who joined in Nursery and left the school in Year 8 during 2012, holding the position of Head Boy during his time here.
Following his time at St Michael’s, Callum attended Tonbridge School as a boarder. He particularly enjoyed getting involved with the sports and volunteering opportunities that the school provided. He completed his undergraduate degree at the University of Bath, followed by a Masters at Imperial College London.
He now works in Project Finance at SMBC Group, covering digital infrastructure assets such as data centre, fibre and telecoms.
Callum is a big sports fan and enjoys spending time with his family, playing with dogs, travelling and capturing landscape photography. He currently lives in London with his brother, Liam, who was in the year below him at St Michael’s.
Emma Sharman
Emma was a parent at St Michael’s Prep for 13 years with both her daughter and son starting in Nursery and leaving at the end of Year 8. During her time at St Michael’s, Emma was part of our P&F Committee as well as volunteering as a Class Representative. Emma is a solicitor by profession, having worked at Allen & Overy in London and Stephenson Harwood in Hong Kong where she and her husband lived for 5 years. Emma is now a full-time mum but has more recently trained as a mediator with Maidstone Mediation. She is a keen rugby and cricket supporter (she is a life member of Gloucestershire County Cricket Club) and enjoys spending time with her family, walking with her Cocker Spaniel, reading, playing tennis and travelling. Emma has been a St Michael’s Governor since 2016.
Jonathan Lidiard
Jon is currently Deputy Head Pastoral and Designated Safeguarding Lead at Sevenoaks School, roles he combines with Classics teaching and rugby coaching. His previous roles have included Housemaster, Head of Department and coach of various different sports. Jon is a keen runner and more broadly a lover of nature and the outdoors, where he tries to spend as much time as possible alongside his wife and three young children.
Jon is looking forward to contributing to the ongoing success and development of St Michael’s as a Governor, and also to immersing himself in the school community, not least as a supporter on the edge of the sports field.
Hayley McLintock
Hayley is an accomplished professional with a diverse background in investment banking, project management and language studies. A passion for education led her to enter teaching in 2004, where she has since dedicated her time to helping young people achieve their full potential. Hayley is currently the Deputy Head - Admissions and Communications at Tonbridge School.
Hayley has taught across five key stages in both state and independent settings, acquiring Specialist Teacher and Assessor status while at Tonbridge. Her leadership roles in special educational needs provision, and the expansion and development of an outstanding Learning Strategies Department at Tonbridge, have been especially noteworthy.
She has a proven track record in delivering exceptional professional development, and has written and delivered several metacognition and community programmes including the ‘Mindset for Success’ and ‘Learning Mentors’ schemes. Her expertise is invaluable to students, teachers and parents.
The Chair of Governors is Mr Rashid Chinchanwala. All governors can be contacted by email at clerktogovernors@stmichaels.kent.sch.uk or in writing, addressed to the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents and Friends - St Michael's Prep School
pageCache.text:
Parents and Friends
St Michael’s Parents and Friends Association (P & F) is a hard working group of volunteer parents committed to supporting the school and its children through fundraising and community building activities.
The group arrange a range of social activities including the Christmas Bazaar, Biennial Ball, Circus, Quiz Nights and Movie Nights. These events are organised to raise funds for additional resources and equipment to enrich the children’s experiences at St Michael’s and raise funds for selected external charities.
Examples of how the funds have been used in the school include creating an extensive adventure playground in the school grounds, part funding of school vehicles, providing Christmas trees for Prep and Pre-Prep as well as extensive Sports, Music, Drama and Science equipment.
The P & F coordinate with volunteer Parent Representatives in classes across the school. The Reps do an invaluable job, liaising with parents to keep them informed of school activities, organising events and providing an efficient method for class/year communications.
The P & F have chosen the Classlist app as an efficient way to connect parents, communicate and promote upcoming events in a way that it is compliant with GDPR. All new joiners to the School will receive further details, but you can join by downloading the Classlist app on iOS or Android and selecting St Michael’s Prep School Parents & Friends Association to sign up. Classlist's Privacy Notice can be found here.
The P & F also use Ticketsource, an online ticketing software provider, for some of their events. The Privacy Notice for Ticketsource can be found here.
For more information or to join St Michael’s P & F, please contact stmichaelspreppf@gmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care - St Michael's Prep School
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
At St Michael’s Prep School, we understand how difficult it can be to tie in school hours with work and other commitments, so we are delighted to offer our families wrap around care.
The clubs are run by qualified and experienced members of St Michael’s Prep staff and your children are looked after in a safe and secure environment where they socialise with friends and take part in a wide variety of creative activities.
Before School Care
Early Risers (Pre-School) - Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 7.30am-8.15am
From September 2026, we are delighted to introduce Early Risers, providing a warm, safe and familiar start to the day for our Pre-School children. Available on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 7.30am-8.15am during term time, children are cared for by qualified and experienced members of St Michael's staff. They have the opportunity to socialise and play with friends before being accompanied to their classroom, helping them to begin the school day feeling happy and settled.
Breakfast Club (Reception to Year 8) - Monday to Friday 7.30am-8.00am
Breakfast Club takes place Monday to Friday 7.30am-8.00am during term time. During this time the children have access to our Hive room and garden: they enjoy breakfast whilst playing with friends and preparing for their school day.
After School Care
The Mini-Hive (Pre-School) - Monday to Friday 4.00-6.00pm
The Pre-School learning day finishes at 3.20pm. If you require a little extra time, you can book our complimentary Relax and Unwind session which runs for 30 minutes and must be booked in advance.
Additional wrap around care is available through the Mini-Hive. This service can be booked by the hour, for a maximum of two hours per day, Monday to Friday 4.00pm to 6.00pm during term time.
Children are cared for by qualified and experienced members of St Michael's staff in a familiar and safe environment where they can socialise with friends and enjoy a variety of creative activities whilst they unwind from the school day. A freshly prepared sandwich tea is provided.
The Hive (Reception to Year 8) - Monday to Friday 4.00-6.30pm
The Hive is open Monday to Friday 4.00pm-6.30pm during term time. In the Hive our children enjoy a plethora of creative activities and games whilst learning new skills including sewing and baking. Every day in the Hive is different and filled with fun!
For further details please contact St Michael's Wrap Around Care Manager, Mrs Nicky Smith at:
wraparoundcare@stmichaels.kent.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: School of Sport - St Michael's Prep School
pageCache.text:
School of Sport
St Michael’s School of Sport is a paid programme offering after school co-curricular sports activities. These sessions are led by an experienced coach possessing a minimum level 2 sports specific qualification.
The primary focus is to provide StMichael’s Prep pupils with the opportunity todevelop their techniques, skills and game play in a safe and fun environment. Our activities encourage the children to explore sports and activities without the fear of failure; fostering agenuine passion for physical activities in them. St Michael’s School of Sport has been in operation since 2021 with both St Michael’s teachers and external coaches leading the after-school sessions. Limited slots are available for these sessions, ensuring that high-quality expert instruction is maintained and that pupils have plenty of opportunities for purposeful practice.
The School of Sport schedule aligns with the curriculum and some sessions run throughout the school year.
The sports covered include Hockey, Football, Rugby, Cricket, Tennis and Gymnastics. Moreover, we have established strong connections with local clubs such as HC Knole Park (Hockey), Sevenoaks Rugby Club, Chipstead FC, Lightning Gymnastics and Love-sport Tennis Club. We are always looking to grow the variety of sports provided by our School of Sport, so the pupils find a sport they love.
If you have any questions about St Michael’s School of Sport and how to access the sessions, please contact schoolofsport@stmichaels.kent.sch.uk

Senior Schools and 11 Plus
Destination Schools
We are proud of the variety of senior schools that our children go to and work closely with parents to choose the right school for their child from Year 5.
Please click here to view our Destinations Schools Booklet which provides details of the senior schools St Michael's pupils are offered places to.
2019-2026 Destinations at 11+

2019-2026 Destinations at 13+
Please click here to view our 2019-2026 destinations at 13+.
11+ (Kent Test)
At St Michael’s Prep the option to take the 11+ (Kent Test) is open to every child in Year 6.
During the Lent and Trinity Terms in Year 5, parents meet with our Head, Deputy Head Academic and our Head of Examinations so that we can support each family with their senior school choices. We will advise of the likelihood of their child passing the test and support the decision of the family as to whether or not the child is entered. Referring the average CAT score can be a useful indicator in our discussions but it does not define the result.
Children leave St Michael’s Prep to a range of senior schools and this information also affects who decides to sit the 11+ examination. Independent senior schools do not require applicants to sit the 11+ which may also factor into the decision and our results. Each cohort and each individual is different; our personalised support helps families to make their decision.
